purpose: Prove across the real network and storage seams that Sender removal and Portal acknowledgement share one durability meaning for data and control messages: nothing staged is lost before its receipt, identical retries stay byte-identical and get the identical receipt, no receipt precedes the Portal's committed archival, and Last Delivery advances from the Portal receipt time of each newly accepted message only. The proof runs the published Sender units against the Portal ingress over HTTP through the Sender HTTP transport, whose network-seam behaviour it pins: exact bytes sent only to the given URL, no redirect followed, one timeout over the whole exchange, a bounded response read, and any incomplete exchange reported as no response.

inputs.name: operator_intent
inputs.description: The Operator's enrollment offer and confirmation of the synthetic installation in the Portal.

inputs.name: staged_messages
inputs.description: Outbox Messages staged by the published Sender units, sealed under the installation key in the Sender's SQLite database.

inputs.name: fetch
inputs.description: The platform fetch the Sender HTTP transport performs each request with.

inputs.name: network
inputs.description: The TCP path between Sender and Portal, which may lose a request, lose or truncate a response, reset a connection, stall, or redirect.

inputs.name: portal_ingress
inputs.description: The Portal ingress shell's enrollment-confirmation, capabilities, and Outbox Message routes, running the published accept and installation units through one writer.

inputs.name: portal_store
inputs.description: The Portal's Operational Store, which the accept units archive into and the proof reads.

outputs.name: http_transport
outputs.description: A Sender HTTP transport serving send-outbox-message@1's and manage-sender-enrollment@1's transport seams: one fetch per request with the exact method, URL, headers, and body bytes, no redirect followed, one timeout over the whole exchange, at most maxResponseBytes + 1 body bytes read, the body returned whatever the HTTP status, and every rejection, timeout, redirect, or incomplete body reported as no response.

outputs.name: durability_evidence
outputs.description: Executable evidence that every staged message is either still in the Sender Outbox or archived byte for byte by the Portal, that every request for a sequence carries identical bytes and every receipt for it is identical, that the Sender removes a message only after the Portal committed it, and that Last Delivery equals the Portal receipt time of the latest newly accepted message.

observable_effects.name: portal-http-request
observable_effects.description: Performs exactly one HTTP request per transport call, to the given URL only.

owns: the end-to-end evidence that Sender removal and Portal acknowledgement share one durability meaning for data and control messages

the network-seam behaviour of the Sender HTTP transport that this evidence relies on: exact request bytes, the given URL only, no redirects, one timeout over the whole exchange, a bounded response read, and incomplete exchanges reported as no response
does_not_own: wire schemas, message identity, and receipt interpretation, which belong to ingest-protocol
staging, sealing, sequences, and the Outbox, which belong to stage-outbox-batch and the other stage units
delivery attempts, receipt-bound removal, and head blocks, which belong to send-outbox-message
the Portal's answers and archival, which belong to accept-ingest-batch, accept-sync-completion, accept-sync-checkpoint, and accept-capability-acknowledgement
enrollment and capability adoption, which belong to manage-sender-enrollment and manage-sender-installation
the Portal route, decompression, request limits, and Authorized Ingress, which belong to the Portal ingress shell
writing the HTTP client module, TLS, and Tailscale reachability, which the Sender shell enabling task provides; this unit pins only the behaviour its evidence relies on
when and how often to attempt delivery, which belongs to coordinate-sender-sync and the Sender shell
